[0] everyday_reading (E): In the everyday sense, 'mouse pressed' is an event the program waits for. StdDraw.mousePressed() only reports whether the button is down at the moment of the call.
[1] misconception (M) -> MouseIsEvent: wrong rule: StdDraw.mousePressed() waits until the user clicks. Right rule: mousePressed() returns immediately with true or false for that moment. To catch clicks, poll it on every frame of a loop.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> MouseIsEvent: Points to LT (each frame polls mousePressed, mouseX and mouseY once). An uneven trace treats one poll as blocking, or reuses an old position on some frames. (here mixing in: "StdDraw.mousePressed() waits until the user clicks")

[0] names_the_element (N): Mouse interaction is the StdDraw input methods mousePressed(), mouseX() and mouseY(), which report the mouse state in user coordinates.
[1] states_the_rule (S): mousePressed() returns whether the button is currently pressed. mouseX() and mouseY() return the latest pointer position in the current x/y scale.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Inside the animation loop: poll the mouse, update state from it, clear, draw, show(t). The mouse is sampled once per frame.
[1] output_prediction (OP): mousePressed() returns a boolean, and mouseX()/mouseY() return doubles in drawing coordinates (e.g. 0.5, 0.5 at the centre of the default canvas).
[2] one_step_execution (OS): A poll changes no state and does not wait. It returns the current mouse state.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Mouse checks run inside the frame loop. A click shorter than one frame (show(t) pause) can be missed.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan: polling loop. The mouse coordinates are most-recent holders updated every frame.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> MouseIsEvent: Changing the frame pause changes how responsive the program is to clicks, but not what a click does.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use mouse polling for interactive drawings and games built on StdDraw. For text dialogue, use StdIn.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: mousePressed() does not block. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Calling mousePressed() once outside a loop: it returns false before the user can click, and the click is ignored.
wrong: StdDraw.mousePressed() waits until the user clicks. | right: mousePressed() only reports whether the button is down at that moment, so it is checked repeatedly in a loop.
Mouse checks run inside the animation loop.
Mouse position and clicks are read through StdDraw methods such as StdDraw.mousePressed().
